items.title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
items.title_zh: 面向 Agentic AI 的可认证执行框架：推理与行动之间的 Petri 网监督控制
items.raw_content: The paper models an LLM agent's tool-execution harness as a Petri-net supervisory control problem in which marks represent capabilities, approvals and budgets, so an injected request with unmet preconditions is refused regardless of wording. It also analyzes a replanning loop in which each retry costs an inference call.

items.title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
items.raw_content:
Authors: Miguel Mochizuki Silva, Samuel Ismael, Mateus C. Dias, Thaís Gaudêncio, Yuri Malheiros et al.

Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage. Methods: An 18-document corpus and an 18-query development benchmark, with one Yes/No or WH-question per document, were used. Retrieval combined dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking. Chunk sizes of 128 to 1024 tokens, overlaps of 0 to 20%, and four retriever configurations were evaluated. Relevance was defined by evidence spans mapped to all containing chunks, treating overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence as relevant. Retrieval was evaluated using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG@K. Separately, generation was assessed on a 512-token index at K=1 to 5 using DeepEval claim-level metrics, with deepseek-v4-pro as the LLM judge, and BLEU/ROUGE metrics. Results: The selected hybrid retriever, using 384-token chunks and 20% overlap, retrieved accepted evidence in the top three results for 17 of 18 queries. Recall@3, R-Precision, MRR@3, and nDCG@3 each reached 0.94. Ground-truth curation increased evidence spans from 25 to 37 and accepted chunk targets from 36 to 51 without changing retrieval rankings. Conclusion: Cross-encoder reranking achieved the highest retrieval scores. Expanded relevance annotations increased recognized evidence without changing rankings, highlighting annotation sensitivity. The small development set and retrieval-informed curation require independent validation, including radiologist assessment of evidence sufficiency.

items.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
items.raw_content: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations October 22, 2026 Flint-interactive gives AI agents a language for creating interactive visualizations. Click a chart, filter data, highlight related content, and explore beyond the view the author originally chose.

items.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
items.raw_content:
Authors: Aleph Alpha, :, Moritz Althaus, Artur Baranowski, Michael Barlow et al.

This report introduces Kolibri, an English-German mixture-of-experts transformer with 78.1B total parameters and 3.46B active parameters per token, released as open weights under the Apache 2.0 licence. We built Kolibri for sovereign and specialised deployment, with a particular focus on German and on regulated domains such as public administration, industry, and aerospace. To support these settings, we control the full model-development process, including data, architecture, training infrastructure, post-training, and evaluation.
  We train Kolibri on 24T tokens across pre-training, mid-training, and long-context extension, with German accounting for more than 20% of the data mix by bytes. To reach this share, we complement German datasets with more than 2T German tokens that we curate from the web with our own pipeline and generate synthetically. Post-training combines supervised fine-tuning on curated German and English data with reinforcement learning on more than 1.2M internally curated tasks, which cover reasoning, tool use, instruction following, code, and retrieval. The model activates 4.4% of its parameters per token, and among the open models evaluated in this report, it lies on the Pareto frontier of quality and serving cost in English and German.
  Kolibri builds on Kolibri Origin, an earlier iteration that validated our full pipeline at scale. Both models come from our Model Factory, which connects data, experimentation, training, evaluation, and deployment through version-controlled workflows.

items.title: Latent Coherence: Do Frontier Language Models' Probability Judgments Obey the Law of Total Probability?
items.raw_content:
Authors: Peter Potash

LawZero's Scientist AI trains a Predictor toward the Bayesian posterior, with an objective that penalizes inconsistent probabilities among latent explanations. We ask whether current frontier language models, with no such training, are already consistent in this sense zero-shot: do their probability judgments satisfy the law of total probability, $P(X)=\sum_z P(z)P(X|z)$, when the latent $z$ must be inferred from records in the context? In separate single-turn calls, models are asked for $P(X)$, for $P(z)$ over the latent's states, and for $P(X|z)$; a causal family applies the same test to $P(y|do(x))$ and the back-door adjustment. Every query has an exact ground-truth probability, and a subset of items is asked in three wordings to separate persistent incoherence from rewording noise. Across seven models, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 are the most coherent (mean absolute residual 0.08 and 0.12 log-odds, about 2 percentage points). Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash and DeepSeek V4-Pro show persistent incoherence (0.27-0.35 log-odds) that is mostly item-specific rather than a shared offset. Within every model, larger residuals go with larger errors against the truth (Spearman 0.40-0.62), so the residual, which needs no ground truth, flags unreliable answers. Reasoning length does not predict coherence, across models or within a model across rewordings of the same question. Simple consistency checks pass almost everywhere; the failures are specific to reasoning through a latent variable. Code and data: https://github.com/ppotash/latent-coherence

items.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
items.raw_content:
Authors: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du

Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory. We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. We propose storing n-gram embeddings at low precision and systematically investigate different quantization methods and bit allocations across tables. Across nanochat-, Llama-, and GPT-2-family models trained from scratch, four-bit tables save approximately 75% of table memory while preserving more than 99% of the validation-loss improvement from adding the tables. Using fewer bits leads to a larger drop in performance, although we find that a short fine-tuning phase recovers a significant part of this loss. In addition, reinvesting the saved memory in larger tables can improve performance beyond that of the original full-precision tables while still using less memory. These table memory savings also extend to large existing models: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, low-bit tables save 47-55% of table memory, with perplexity increases of less than 1.2% and largely preserved downstream task performance. These findings establish low-bit precision as a practical way to reduce the memory requirements of n-gram embeddings and use the saved capacity to improve model performance.

items.title: Not Every Agent Needs the Strongest Model: Unified Prompt-Model Optimization for Heterogeneous LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.raw_content:
Authors: Mingxiu Cai, Haoyang Xian, Xinyu Ma, Yutong Wang, Zhenxi Song et al.

Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on role-specific prompts and execution models to solve complex tasks collaboratively. However, prompt optimization typically keeps model assignments fixed, leaving differences in role requirements and their associated inference costs outside the search. We present UniMASO, a Unified framework for heterogeneous Multi-Agent System Optimization through the joint adaptation of prompts and model assignments. UniMASO evaluates candidate updates through local, downstream, and global feedback, using cost-aware Pareto search to retain useful quality-cost trade-offs. Topology-aware co-evolution then coordinates these updates according to agent roles and dependencies. Cross-level trajectory memory further supplies historical successes and failures to guide subsequent optimization. Experiments on five benchmarks and five execution topologies show that UniMASO achieves competitive task performance at substantially lower deployment cost than the strongest homogeneous configurations. Under centralized execution, it improves the average score from 69.79 to 70.40 while reducing token-weighted deployment cost by 85.2% relative to DeepSeek-V4-Pro with MASPO. These results support joint prompt-model adaptation as an effective approach to efficient multi-agent collaboration. The code is available at https://github.com/Achilles008/UniMASO_main.

items.title: POS-Signature Demonstration Retrieval for In-Context Dependency Parsing
items.raw_content:
Authors: Muhammad Azam Afridi, Rajab Ali, Marco Passarotti

Demonstrations for in-context learning are often retrieved by semantic similarity, which may be a poor proxy for relevance in structured prediction. We study demonstration selection for Universal Dependencies parsing with a POS-signature policy that represents sentences with weighted part-of-speech statistics and retrieves three length-compatible, gold-parsed examples from the labeled training split. We evaluate two open-weight language models without fine-tuning on all 2,077 sentences of the UD English Web Treebank test set, comparing the policy with shot- and format-matched fixed and semantic three-shot baselines, as well as zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and critique-refinement systems. POS-signature retrieval yields the highest labeled attachment score among the tested prompting systems for both models (72.4 and 73.2), outperforming semantic retrieval by 1.9 and 2.7 points; paired-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals exclude zero for both contrasts. Chain-of-thought and refinement comparisons vary across models. These exploratory results favor the tested POS-signature retrieval approach on English-EWT. We release the prompts, archived outputs, and evaluation code.

items.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning
items.raw_content:
Authors: Akila Ayanthi, Darshana Priyasad, Tharindu Fernando, Sridha Sridharan, Clinton Fookes et al.

Regularisation-based class-incremental learning (CIL) methods control the stability-plasticity trade-off through fixed coefficients tuned offline, independently of the continual learning objective and blind to phase-specific variations in data volume, task difficulty, and class similarity. We argue this is a fundamental mismatch and propose REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning, which treats regularisation strength selection as a sequential decision problem. At each incremental phase, a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) agent observes a compact state of current performance metrics and incoming data statistics, and outputs the distillation coefficients for that phase. To respect CIL's constraint on historical data access, the policy is trained entirely on pseudo-CIL tasks constructed from the initial phase, then deployed on the incremental sequence without further adaptation. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that REDAR reduces forgetting and improves forward transfer over fixed and heuristic baselines, and that policies trained on short pseudo-task horizons transfer effectively to longer incremental runs.

items.title: Which Answer Did the Seventeen-Year-Old Write? A Behavioral Case Study of Author-Age Misattribution, Miscalibrated Confidence, and Non-Corrective Self-Explanation in Six Frontier Language Models
items.raw_content:
Authors: Brianne Lee

Three students answered the same exam prompt by hand: "What is happiness? Are you happy?" Their ages, recorded at collection, are 17, 28, and 45. The 17-year-old's answer is hedged and formally phrased. Asked to match each answer to an age and gender label, most frontier language models confidently assign it to an adult. This paper reports a structured case study of that failure across six models: Claude Fable 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5, GPT-4o (2024), and DeepSeek V4. We ran 1,081 API sessions and scored 3,225 responses across six experimental conditions that manipulate framing, disclosure format, and audience-awareness instruction. Three of six models perform at or near chance (1/3) on the matching task while reporting 73-88% mean confidence. The youngest writer's answer is misattributed to an adult in up to 90% of trials. Removing the multiple-choice scaffold collapses accuracy further: three models never place within three years of the true age once open-ended estimation is required. Institutional framing ("a community-college biology final") significantly degrades the best-performing model's accuracy; a neutral label does not. A single audience-awareness instruction significantly improves one model (+21 points) and moves another to ceiling, with no detectable effect on the three weakest models. Stated confidence is uncorrelated or inversely correlated with correctness for five of six models. After ground truth is revealed, one model names its own stereotyping in 68 of 114 explanations, yet shows the lowest accuracy and highest confidence of any model under blind presentation: articulate retrospective diagnosis that does not track the quality of its judgments. This is a three-item, single-topic, single-language case study meant to isolate a mechanism, not to estimate a population bias rate. Data, code, and raw model outputs are publicly released.

items.title: Qianjue Unveils Polibrain, a Predictive World Model Built to Run Across Robot Body Types
items.title_zh: Qianjue 发布 Polibrain 预测式世界模型，适配多种机器人本体
items.raw_content: Qianjue, a developer of robot brains, launched Polibrain, a world model that predicts task-relevant state changes rather than future video frames and is adapted to quadruped, humanoid and wheeled robots.

items.title: SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs
items.title_zh: SurveyGraph：通过方法—实体知识图谱生成学术综述
items.raw_content: SurveyGraph builds a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph encoding follow-on, competition and shared-resource relations between methods to support core-paper discovery, retrieval and evidence-gated narrative synthesis; in one diagnostic, graph-aware retrieval nearly doubled recall over flat lexical baselines.

items.title: ReCoG: Relational Concept Graph for Training-Free Personalization
items.title_zh: ReCoG：面向免训练个性化的关系概念图
items.raw_content: ReCoG represents personalized concepts as nodes in a graph augmented with directed edges that capture discriminative cues between confusable pairs, then resolves ambiguity at inference through pairwise comparisons; it also introduces the FINGER benchmark for confusable concept sets.

items.title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
items.title_zh: Gate3DGen：为三维生成选择性净化真实世界图像的预处理模型
items.raw_content: Gate3DGen is a selective pre-processing model that bypasses inputs classified as clean and purifies degraded ones before existing single-image 3D generators, using a degradation-aware router and a one-step purifier; on its synthetic benchmark it reduced TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% in about 2.3 seconds on average.

items.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.title_zh: Memory before Goal：预历史记忆在人形机器人全身移动操作中的作用
items.raw_content: WholeBodyMem is an object-guided perceptual memory for whole-body vision-language-action policies that keeps key pre-history frames of task objects. It raised its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on a real Unitree G1, alongside a new HuMeGo benchmark.

items.title: 1Password launches solution for safely using logins with AI agents
items.title_zh: 1Password 推出让 AI agent 安全使用登录凭据的方案
items.raw_content: 1Password launched 1Password for Agents, extending its password-management work for agentic AI after a Claude integration introduced in July.

items.title: ShengShu Livestreams Two Weeks of Motubrain 2.0 Training Ahead of Open-Source Release
items.title_zh: ShengShu 直播 Motubrain 2.0 两周训练过程，开源在即
items.raw_content: ShengShu Technology's world model team began livestreaming the full training of its Motubrain 2.0 embodied model on October 21, a run planned for about two weeks before open-sourcing.
